newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Fairfax says print plant costs hit profit.
newsitem.headline: Fairfax says print plant costs hit profit.

text.p: Newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday the fall in operating profit before abnormals reflected the higher depreciation and interest expense of about A$50 million from the completion of the Chullora printing plant in Sydney.

Fairfax, about 22 percent owned by Brierley Investments Ltd, said pre-abnormal operating profit was A$85 million in the year to June 30, 1997, down from A$102.2 million a year ago. It said annual sales revenues rose 2.8 percent to A$1.02 billion. Second half sales rose 6.3 percent to A$510.9 million.
"This result was encouraging and again demonstrated some improvement in economic conditions and the advertising market particularly in the last few months of the year," Fairfax said.
Analysts had forecast Fairfax to report a net profit before abnormals between A$75.1 million and A$99.4 million for 1996/97, compared with A$102 million a year earlier.

Fairfax, which publishes the Sydney Morning Hearld, The Age and business daily The Australian Financial Review, said total newspaper advertising revenues were 2.7 percent up on the 1995/96 year with improved yields offset by lower volumes.
It said total net circulation revenues were up 0.7 percent reflecting improved circulation results achieved, mainly in the major publications, and the benefits of cover price increases.

Australia's oldest newspaper group said total costs rose 1.5 percent to A$770 million. The higher costs were due to increased marketing costs and higher newsprint costs associated with more page volumes.
Fairfax said net debt was reduced by A$54 million during the year taking the debt to equity ratio to 75 percent at June 30, compared with 80 percent a year earlier.
It said the abnormal charge of A$16.40 million included the employee redundancy and executive severance costs of A$3.6 million and A$7.4 million in restructuring costs.
At 4.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), Fairfax shares were one cent down at A$3.18, compared with A$3.21 before the results announcement.
